reviews.review:
I will mainly be talking about the single-player, so up to this day the GTA I liked the least among Vice City, IV and San Andreas I am not taking into account the 2D era. To begin, the story is heavily inspired by heist movies like Heat. You take control of three criminals who have to carry out a marathon of robberies against a backdrop of conflicts and unspoken tensions. The gameplay in the chase sequences is completely scripted. The story is simple and not memorable; the writing is decent, but we're still looking for iconic characters with cheeky lines. I wonder where Rockstar Games' humor has gone. The characters are all bland and lack personality; it's more hipster writing than what we're used to seeing.

The fact that you can play as three characters simultaneously is something I didn't like because it breaks a certain dynamic, and the characters are less developed. I'm not interested in playing as Franklin, who isn't developed at all. I was really disappointed by the lack of missions in his neighborhood and with his gang. He has an immeasurable lack of charisma. [spoiler]He's practically erased from the story. If I'd had the choice to kill him at the end, I would have chosen him without a doubt.[/spoiler] Trevor, on the other hand, is a good character that I wish I hadn't played as, but rather visited for missions. I compare him to Phil Cassidy, a bit of a crazy guy. Trevor was added during development, according to Dan Houser, there was no intention of controlling him. That shows how underdeveloped the story is. The real and best-developed character is Michael (inspired by Tony Soprano's life), the most interesting because he has a connection to the ghetto through Franklin and to the desert/country through Trevor. It's Michael who connects people; he's the most charismatic character and the one who truly carries GTA V, in addition to having impeccable voice acting. A GTA without DLC, with far less missions (79 missions) than San Andreas (101 missions) and GTA IV + DLCs (136 missions), a little over 10 more missions than Vice City (67 missions), a game from 2002. Isn't there a slight problem considering we play as three characters?

The late 2010s, with Rockstar Games and Take-Two influencing the video game world, marked the beginning of an era where studios focused on online play, where fewer and fewer people played single-player games. As a result, we ended up with games where single-player was neglected in favor of online mode, as perfectly exemplified by GTA V. In the 2000s, multiplayer appeared in the menu after the single-player campaign; today, games shove online mode right in your face. Studios that have become focused solely on online play, a lack of single-player DLC, microtransactions, endless updates, and an over-exploitation of online mode given the profit it generates. Red Dead Redemption 2 is the exception, but keep in mind that it's the only Rockstar game developed for 4th-generation consoles. The online mode was cool in the early years because it focused on creating lasting memories. You can't take that away from them.

But the writing is gone, the online experience has become terrible, and the people in charge of the script are a disgrace. It's worth noting that they censored original content from the solo; if you want to see the list, it's amusing. They believe they have the right to change the game because it is offensive. The fact that GTA is the most played and best-selling game of all time attracts people who don't intend to play a game, but to control it. So I'm asking for all the grafitti to be removed from the game because I feel bad against. Seriously, no jokes, this is getting ridiculous. It's the same reason I'm not playing the remastered versions of the 3D trilogy.

Rockstar Games has lost many people since its creation who were part of its DNA. I'm thinking of Dan Houser, Leslie Benzies, Jamie King, Terry Donovan, Lazlow Jones, Michael Unsworth, Rupert Humphries, David Jones, Obbe Vermeij ...
